elements.element: Customer may assign this Agreement to an affiliate without consent.
elements.evidence: Section (d) facially permits this upon written notice, but unchanged section (c) separately prohibits assignment absent Garman's written authorization. Because section (d) does not expressly override section (c), and section (c)'s subject is omitted from the excerpt, the Customer's unqualified consent-free right is not demonstrably operative.

elements.element: Customer may assign this Agreement without consent to a successor in connection with a merger.
elements.evidence: Section (d) includes this right, but section (c)'s unchanged written-authorization requirement creates an unresolved conflicting restriction. The margin comment cannot make section (c) subject to section (d).

elements.element: Customer may assign this Agreement without consent to a successor in connection with an acquisition.
elements.evidence: Section (d) includes acquisition successors, but the unchanged assignment prohibition in section (c) prevents the consent-free right from being demonstrably effective.

elements.element: Customer may assign this Agreement without consent to a successor in connection with a sale of all or substantially all assets.
elements.evidence: Section (d) contains the required substantially-all-assets carve-out, but section (c) still requires Garman's written authorization and is not operatively subordinated to section (d).

elements.element: Vendor may assign this Agreement only with Customer's consent.
elements.evidence: Section (d) permits Vendor, as either party, to assign without consent to an affiliate or qualifying transaction successor.

elements.element: Where Customer consent to a Vendor assignment is required, Customer may not unreasonably withhold that consent.
elements.evidence: Section (d) provides that the other party's required consent may not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned or delayed, which applies to Customer consent for Vendor assignments outside the carve-outs.

elements.element: Vendor may never assign this Agreement to a Customer competitor.
elements.evidence: No competitor prohibition appears. Section (d) could permit a consented assignment to a competitor and could also permit a consent-free assignment where the competitor is a qualifying affiliate or successor.

elements.element: Vendor has no termination right triggered by Customer's change of control.
elements.evidence: Neither operative provision grants Vendor a termination right based on Customer's change of control.

elements.element: Customer may assign this Agreement to a successor without consent.
elements.evidence: Section (d) facially grants the right for specified transaction successors, but section (c)'s unchanged written-authorization requirement creates an unresolved conflict, so Customer's consent-free right is not demonstrably effective.

elements.element: Customer must provide written notice when assigning this Agreement to a successor.
elements.evidence: Section (d) conditions the successor-assignment carve-out on written notice to the other party.

elements.element: Vendor may assign this Agreement to a successor without consent.
elements.evidence: Section (d) facially grants this right, but section (c) remains an operative assignment restriction and its omitted subject prevents the conflict from being conclusively allocated away from Vendor.

elements.element: Vendor must provide written notice when assigning this Agreement to a successor.
elements.evidence: Section (d) requires either party to provide written notice for an assignment to a qualifying successor.

elements.element: Customer assignments other than assignments to successors require Vendor's consent.
elements.evidence: Section (d) allows Customer to assign to an affiliate without consent even where the affiliate is not a successor.

elements.element: Vendor may not unreasonably withhold consent to Customer assignments for which consent is required.
elements.evidence: Section (d) expressly states that the other party's required consent may not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned or delayed.

elements.element: Vendor assignments other than assignments to successors require Customer's consent.
elements.evidence: Section (d) allows Vendor to assign to an affiliate without consent even where the affiliate is not a successor.

elements.element: Customer may not unreasonably withhold consent to Vendor assignments for which consent is required.
elements.evidence: Section (d) expressly applies the reasonableness standard mutually to required assignment consent.

result.reason: The redline does not reach the preferred position because it gives Vendor consent-free affiliate and successor rights and contains no competitor prohibition. It also does not reach the fallback because non-successor affiliate assignments are exempted from consent. In addition, unchanged section (c) still requires Garman's written authorization for assignment and is not operatively made subject to section (d); the margin comment cannot cure that contradiction. The extra mutual affiliate carve-out is unnecessary for the fallback and contrary to the preferred allocation, so the redline is not minimal and does not reliably preserve the intended assignment regime.
